title: Core existence for a regular complete finite subring
statement: A complete local Noetherian domain admits a regular complete local subring over which it is finite.

proof.text: Obtain the equal-dimension parameter algebra A and its Hausdorff target and finite reduction. The field/Cohen power-series theorem supplies regularity, completeness and the domain property of A.

Apply the finite-over-complete-ring theorem to the maximal ideal of A and the A-module R, giving finite generation of R over A. Restrict to the image B of A in R; the inclusion B → R is finite by Mathlib RingHom.Finite.of_comp_finite.

Finiteness gives integrality by Mathlib Algebra.IsIntegral.of_finite. Incomparability (Ideal.IsIntegral.comap_lt_comap) makes contraction on prime spectra strictly monotone, so dim R ≤ dim B by Order.krullDim_le_of_strictMono. If the parameter map killed a nonzero x, the source domain makes x a nonzerodivisor and ringKrullDim_succ_le_of_surjective gives dim B + 1 ≤ dim A. Equal dimensions then give dim R + 1 ≤ dim R. The power-series dimension is a natural number, so ENat.WithBot.add_one_le_natCast_iff yields an impossible strict self-inequality. Thus the map is injective.

The bijective range restriction gives a ring equivalence A ≃ B. Transport regularity with IsRegularLocalRing.of_ringEquiv; transport maximal-ideal-adic completeness with map_ringEquiv_maximalIdeal and IsAdicComplete.congr_ringEquiv. The already proved finiteness of B → R gives Module.Finite B R.

proof_origin.place: Coefficient/parameter construction split off; finite generation, dimension injectivity and range identification formalized from existing declarations and Mathlib
